intro: Paste the week's log and its quadrant distribution, followed by the 250–350 word write-up including your position on this module's claim. Resubmission is free and unlimited — the score is a mirror, not a gate.
activityContext: You are grading a learner submission for AI 301 · The Specialist, HRBP track. Module 2 applied activity, 'One week, sorted': a real week logged (last week, not a representative one, including interrupt-driven work that never hit a calendar), every item sorted into four quadrants using two questions — does it require presence, does it require contested judgment — with split hours where a block spans quadrants, a resulting percentage distribution, one piece of work they will defend against automation with reasoning, one they will surrender, and a comparison against their predicted presence-or-contested share. The write-up must state a position on the module's claim — that core work being hard for AI is not job security, because the ratio moves when the easy half compresses — and address the strongest counter-argument, which is that ratios are set by budget appetite and proximity-to-business value rather than by workload math. Key grading insight: presence is not seniority and contested judgment is not difficulty; the most common error is filing calendar inheritance (the ritual) or determinate-but-hard work as irreducible. This track scores the delta rather than the score — never grade prediction accuracy.

opening.label: Predicted — % of your week needing presence or contested judgment

calibration.label: Measured — the share your logged week actually shows
calibration.hint: Room plus ritual plus desk, from your own distribution.

dimensions.name: The week is real
dimensions.criteria: An actual week rather than a typical one, including the interrupt-driven work that never reaches a calendar, with approximate hours. A messy honest week outscores a tidy representative one, and admitting untracked time outscores rounding it away.

dimensions.name: Both questions actually applied
dimensions.criteria: Each item classified against presence AND contest explicitly, with blocks split across quadrants rather than rounded to the flattering one. Watch for the two named errors — treating seniority as presence, treating difficulty as contest — and say so plainly in feedback where they appear.

dimensions.name: The surrender is genuine
dimensions.criteria: The defended item carries a reason beyond 'it's important.' The surrendered item is real work they currently spend judgment-grade attention on — this is the harder and more valuable half, and a surrender that costs the learner nothing should score low.

dimensions.name: The position and the delta
dimensions.criteria: A committed position on the compression claim that engages the budget-appetite counter-argument rather than a weaker one, plus the prediction compared, miss direction named, and a specific account of what would have to stop for five points to move from queue to room. Accuracy of the prediction is not graded.
